Regulation: B.C. Reg. 154/2026
Made under: Motor Vehicle Act
Published in: No. 16 – B.C. Regs. 153 to 162, September 22, including September 8, 2026
Deposit date: September 10, 2026

B.C. Reg. 154/2026, deposited September 10, 2026, under theMOTOR VEHICLE ACT[section 83.1 (8)]. Order in Council 395/2026, approved and ordered September 10, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective September 30, 2026, the Motor Vehicle Act Regulations, B.C. Reg. 26/58, are amended as set out in the attached Schedule. — N. KRIEGER,Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General; J. WICKENS,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Section 41.01 of the Motor Vehicle Act Regulations, B.C. Reg. 26/58, is amended (a)	by repealing subsection (1.1) and substituting the following: (1.1)	For the purpose of prescribing a speed monitoring device under section 83.1 (8) (a) of the Act, the following are prescribed: (a)	the JENOPTIK TraffiStar SR391plus; (b)	the REDFLEX-HALO-FIXED-1.3-12MPDUAL., and (b)	in subsection (2) by adding the following paragraph: (b.1)	the JENOPTIK TraffiStar SR391plus;. minutes_briefs.title: BC approves two new speed cameras, including one that can ticket vehicles in both directions
minutes_briefs.summary: BC has amended the Motor Vehicle Act Regulations to add two new approved speed monitoring devices: the JENOPTIK TraffiStar SR391plus and the REDFLEX-HALO-FIXED-1.3-12MPDUAL. The change took effect September 30, 2026. These are the cameras police and the province use to catch and ticket speeding vehicles. Adding them to the approved list means tickets issued from these devices are legally valid in BC.
